content: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). If the symptoms are not life-threatening, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. Before starting this medication and during its use, laboratory and/or medical tests should be conducted. These tests may include assessments of kidney and liver function, as well as blood mineral levels such as calcium, magnesium, and potassium. It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. It is crucial to take each dose of this medication as prescribed. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage, refer to the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for specific details. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Posaconazole, commonly sold under the brand name Noxafil, is used to prevent certain fungal infections in patients with severely weakened immune systems, such as those undergoing chemotherapy. It belongs to a class of drugs known as azole antifungals. Before using posaconazole, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. This medication is typically administered by injection into a vein, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure you have been thoroughly trained by your healthcare professional on its preparation and usage. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. Do not use the liquid if either is present. This medication is most effective when its levels in the body are maintained consistently. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, abdominal pain, dizziness, or difficulty sleeping. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, posaconazole may cause severe (potentially fatal) liver disease. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are also rare. Posaconazole may commonly cause a mild rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using posaconazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other azole antifungals (such as ketoconazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Posaconazole may cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that may cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase your risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be heightened if you use certain drugs (such as diuretics or water pills) or if you experience conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This drug may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. Discuss with your doctor if you are using marijuana (cannabis). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of posaconazole from your body, which could impact how posaconazole works. Similarly, this drug may slow the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially affecting their efficacy. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, the poison control center can be reached at 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as kidney/liver function and blood mineral levels like calcium, magnesium, and potassium) should be conducted before starting this medication and during its use. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule.
